properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 10 at 9:29AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall that has occurred upstream has resulted in river
levels just below Moderate flood stage. River levels are expected to
remain steady near Moderate Flood stage through this week and into
the weekend as a large volume of water works north through the basin.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated. At 3.0 feet, Water
approaches or may enter lowest homes on or near Wildhog Road and
nearby canals. Flooding reaches the parking lot of the Juno Trail
Apartments. Flooding on portions of Alligator Road and Holiday
Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue Creek are flooded. Roads at
Astor Landing Campground and Lake Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood.
Water enters lower homes closest to the river on McPherson Lane.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EST Tuesday the stage was 2.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EST Tuesday was 2.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise slightly to 3 feet late
this week. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EST.

properties.description:

caused Major flooding at the gauge west of Cocoa. Water levels
continue to slowly rise at upstream gauges. The river is forecast to
remain within Major flood stage through this week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 AM EST Tuesday the stage was 17.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:15 AM EST Tuesday was 17.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to continue rising, cresting at
17.2 feet this weekend.

properties.areaDesc: Goliad; Victoria; Inland Refugio; Inland Calhoun; Coastal Refugio; Coastal Calhoun; Calhoun Islands
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 10 at 8:06AM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
At 806 AM CST, Doppler radar was tracking an area of strong
thunderstorms extending from over Salem to over Indianola, or
extending from 11 miles north of Victoria to near Port Oconnor,
moving northeast at 35 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph and pea size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Victoria, Port Lavaca, Seadrift, McFaddin, Port Oconnor, Guadalupe,
Point Comfort, Placedo, Dacosta, Bloomington, Wood Hi, Green Lake,
Telferner, Brentwood Subdivision, Victoria Regional Airport, Long
Mott, Victoria Colony Creek Country Club, Victoria College,
Downtown Victoria and Tivoli.

This includes the following highways...
US Highway 59 between mile markers 622 and 654. US Highway 183 near
mile marker 628. US Highway 77 between mile markers 558 and 598. US
Highway 87 between mile markers 796 and 840.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.

Frequent cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.
Lightning can strike 10 miles away from a thunderstorm. Seek a safe
shelter inside a building or vehicle.

NWSheadline: AN AREA OF STRONG THUNDERSTORMS WILL IMPACT NORTHEASTERN GOLIAD... CALHOUN...NORTHEASTERN REFUGIO AND VICTORIA COUNTIES UNTIL 845 AM CST

properties.areaDesc: Duval, TX; Jim Wells, TX; Kleberg, TX; Nueces, TX; San Patricio, TX; Webb, TX
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 10 at 7:59AM CST until November 10 at 11:00AM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southern Duval County in south central Texas...
Jim Wells County in south central Texas...
Kleberg County in south central Texas...
Nueces County in south central Texas...
Southern San Patricio County in south central Texas...
Southeastern Webb County in south central Texas...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM CST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 759 AM CST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Overflowing poor drainage areas will cause minor
flooding in the advisory area. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain has
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Corpus Christi, Kingsville, Alice, Portland, Robstown, San Diego,
Premont, Benavides, Driscoll, Corpus Christi International
Airport, Ingleside, Bishop, Ingleside On The Bay, Ben Bolt, Alice
Acres, Palito Blanco and Kingsville Naval Air Station.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.areaDesc: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Mayaguez and Vicinity; Culebra
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 10 at 9:21AM AST until November 11 at 6:00AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...High Rip Current Risk, life-threatening rip currents.

* WHERE...North-facing beaches of Puerto Rico, including Culebra.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Lingering northerly swells generated by
distant surface low over the central Atlantic will support
breaking waves of 5 to 7 feet and a high risk of life-
threatening rip currents along the northern exposed beaches of
Puerto Rico and Culebra.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

NWSheadline: HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH LATE TONIGHT

capable of producing winds to around 30 knots and possible
waterspouts. These strong thunderstorms were over the northern
offshore Atlantic waters, moving north at 10 knots.

waves, lightning strikes, heavy downpours, and possible waterspouts.
Boaters should seek safe harbor immediately until these storms pass.

The National Weather Service in League City has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Freeport to Matagorda Ship Channel TX out 20
NM...
Waters from Freeport to Matagorda Ship Channel TX from 20 to 60
NM...

Galveston A122, Brazos A4, Brazos A26, Matagorda Island 607,
Galveston A171, Brazos A70, and Brazos B133.

turbulent flow can wash motorists, campers, and equipment
downstream from Pafford Crossing to Amistad Reservoir. Livestock
are cut off and potentially drowned below Juno to Amistad
Reservoir.

this afternoon and continue falling to 3.3 feet Sunday morning.
- Flood stage is 5.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 6.2
feet on 10/19/2018.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued November 10 at 2:21AM AKST until November 10 at 12:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK

expected.

* WHERE...Whittier, Portage Valley, and East Turnagain Arm.

vehicles. Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects and a few

properties.description:

expected along west-facing beaches.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until noon PST today. For
the Beach Hazards Statement, through this evening.

isolated road closures expected. Dangerous swimming conditions

astronomical tide predictions.

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water to avoid
hazardous swimming conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Northern Washington Coast; Grays Harbor County Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 10 at 1:28AM PST until November 10 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected. Inundation of 1.5 to 2 feet above ground level is
possible along shorelines and low-lying coastal areas. For the
High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves along the coast.

* WHERE...Northern Washington Coast and Grays Harbor County
Coast zones.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 10 AM this morning
to 3 PM PST this afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, from
10 AM this morning to 10 AM PST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding due to tidal overflow is
expected around high tide. This may lead to flooding of parking
lots, parks, and roads, with only isolated road closures
expected. Large breaking waves can knock people off their feet,
move driftwood and debris, and crash over rocks and jetties.
People can be injured or drown while observing the ocean.
Localized beach and coastal erosion is expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Significant log and debris pile-up on the
beaches and jetties from the high surf last weekend will pose
additional threats to those on the beaches and will exacerbate
coastal erosion.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inundation above ground level refers to the height above the Mean
Higher High Water (MHHW) level.

Never turn your back on the ocean and keep children and pets
close. Know the tides and forecast conditions. Follow warning
signs and respect barriers.

properties.areaDesc: Ernestine
properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 10 at 12:06AM AKST until November 10 at 12:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Mixed precipitation likely. Total snow accumulations between
6 and 12 inches. Ice accumulations around a trace.

* WHERE...Richardson Highway from mile marker 60 and south.

* WHEN...Until noon AKST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Visibility could be
significantly reduced within heavy snow.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Heavy snow is likely through Tuesday morning.
The higher-end snow amounts are expected towards the north side of
Thompson Pass with the lower-end snow totals expected to the north.
Freezing rain potential is decreasing with this system, although it
cannot be fully ruled out. There is a 10 percent or less chance of
freezing rain mixing in with the snow as temperatures look cold
enough for all snow. Tonsina is not expected to see much snow
accumulation from this system.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For the latest road
conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

properties.areaDesc: Interior Kenai Peninsula; Turnagain Pass
properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 10 at 12:06AM AKST until November 10 at 6:00AM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Mixed precipitation likely. Total snow accumulations between
4 and 12 inches. Ice accumulations around a light glaze possible.

* WHERE...Interior Kenai Peninsula and Turnagain Pass.

* WHEN...Until 6 AM AKST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Visibility could be
significantly reduced within heavy snow. Ponding of water along the
Seward Highway is likely due to rain and melting snow overnight
through Tuesday morning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The higher-end snow totals are expected for
Turnagain Pass and Summit Lake areas, where snow will hold on
longer before changing to rain. Any freezing rain that falls will
be short in duration. Valley locations, including Tern Lake to
Moose Pass will see lower snow accumulation and a quicker
transition from snow to rain. Rain on top of snow that has already
fallen may also lead to slush and ponding for water on roads.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For the latest road
conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 10 at 12:06AM AKST until November 10 at 12:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:

3 inches and ice accumulations up to one tenth of an inch. Winds
gusting as high as 45 mph, mainly along the Inlet.

* WHERE...NW Kenai Peninsula, SW Kenai Peninsula, and Skilak Lake.

* WHEN...Until noon AKST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Along the coast, gusty winds
could bring down a few tree branches. Roads, and especially bridges
and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous overnight
into early Tuesday morning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Areas of light snow will transition to
freezing rain before becoming all rain with above freezing
temperatures Tuesday morning. There is increased confidence in a
quicker warm-up, meaning less snow accumulation and a quicker
changeover to rain. Areas at sea level will likely see little snow
accumulation, with most of the accumulation expected at higher
elevations, including the Homer Bluffs.
properties.instruction:

conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Beaches of Volusia, Indian River, Saint Lucie, Martin,
and Brevard Counties.

* WHEN...Through late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 9 at 7:12PM PST until November 10 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal
flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 9 to 14 feet with dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...Until noon PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely.
Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an
increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides of near 7.0 ft (MLLW) are
expected each morning. The High Surf and Coastal Flood
Advisories may need to be extended through the week.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 9 at 9:38AM MST until November 11 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Salt River below Granite Reef Dam is
occurring. Flooding of low water crossings across the Salt River
upstream of Tempe Town Lake, including McKellips Road, is
occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 932 AM MST, dam operators reported over 1000 cfs continues to
be released from Granite Reef Dam. Flooding due to a dam
floodgate release will continue.
- Flooding is occurring along the Salt River.
- Salt River between Granite Reef Dam and Tempe Town Lake.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Flooding is occurring. It is important to know where you are relative
to streams, rivers, or creeks. Campers and hikers should avoid
streams or creeks.
